addmaths-0606-factors-polynomials-operat.description: Expand products and collect signed coefficients by their corresponding powers.

sections.title: Which terms do I combine?
sections.label: Collect
sections.intro: Group terms with matching powers. The coefficient of a missing power is zero.

blocks.html: Add only coefficients of the same power.

blocks.prompt:
Let \(F(x)=(2 x^{2} - 4 x + 3)+(x^{2} + 6 x + 1)\).

Expand and simplify the expression.
blocks.solution:
Group terms with the same power of x.

Write the result from the highest power down to the constant.

Final answer: \(3 x^{2} + 2 x + 4\).
blocks.hint: Group terms with the same power of x.

blocks.html: For subtraction, change every sign inside the second bracket.

blocks.prompt:
Let \(F(x)=(3 x^{2} - 4 x - 3)+(2 x^{2} + 6 x)\).

Expand and simplify the expression.
blocks.solution:
Group terms with the same power of x.

Write the result from the highest power down to the constant.

Final answer: \(5 x^{2} + 2 x - 3\).
blocks.hint: Group terms with the same power of x.

sections.title: How do I subtract a polynomial?
sections.label: Subtract
sections.intro: Regard a subtraction as multiplication of the second bracket by negative one.

blocks.html: After distributing the minus sign, collect like powers.

blocks.prompt:
Let \(F(x)=(2 x^{2} - 5 x)-(x^{2} + 7 x - 3)\).

Expand and simplify the expression.
blocks.solution:
Distribute the minus sign to every term in the second bracket.

Write the result from the highest power down to the constant.

Final answer: \(x^{2} - 12 x + 3\).
blocks.hint: Distribute the minus sign to every term in the second bracket.

blocks.html: Changing the first sign alone is insufficient.

blocks.prompt:
Let \(F(x)=(3 x^{2} - 5 x + 1)-(2 x^{2} + 7 x + 2)\).

Expand and simplify the expression.
blocks.solution:
Distribute the minus sign to every term in the second bracket.

Write the result from the highest power down to the constant.

Final answer: \(x^{2} - 12 x - 1\).
blocks.hint: Distribute the minus sign to every term in the second bracket.

sections.title: How do I keep track of a product?
sections.label: Multiply
sections.intro: Make a list of products before adding the terms. A small multiplication grid can help.

blocks.html: Multiply each term of one bracket by every term of the other.

blocks.prompt:
Let \(F(x)=(2 x^{2} - 6 x - 3)\times(x - 6)\).

State the coefficient of \(x^2\).
blocks.solution:
Use the coefficients after collecting like powers.

The squared term is \(- 18 x^{2}\).

Final answer: \(-18\).
blocks.hint: Use the coefficients after collecting like powers.

blocks.html: When multiplying powers of x, add their exponents.

blocks.prompt:
Let \(F(x)=(3 x^{2} - 6 x - 2)\times(x - 6)\).

State the coefficient of \(x^2\).
blocks.solution:
Use the coefficients after collecting like powers.

The squared term is \(- 24 x^{2}\).

Final answer: \(-24\).
blocks.hint: Use the coefficients after collecting like powers.

addmaths-0606-factors-polynomials-long-d.description: Use a leading-term division, multiplication and subtraction to find a quotient and remainder.

sections.title: Where does the first quotient term come from?
sections.label: Leading term
sections.intro: Compare the highest powers in the dividend and divisor. Divide their terms including their coefficients.

blocks.html: In each step divide, multiply, subtract and repeat.

blocks.prompt:
The polynomial \(P(x)=9 x^{3} - 6 x^{2} + 6 x - 9\) is divided by \(3 x - 3\).

Find the first term of the quotient.
blocks.solution:
Divide the leading term of the dividend by the leading term of the divisor.

The quotient starts with \(3 x^{2}\).

Final answer: \(3\).
blocks.hint: Divide the leading term of the dividend by the leading term of the divisor.

blocks.html: A non-monic divisor also changes the quotient coefficient.

blocks.prompt:
The polynomial \(P(x)=16 x^{3} - 4 x^{2} + 6 x - 8\) is divided by \(4 x - 3\).

Find the first term of the quotient.
blocks.solution:
Divide the leading term of the dividend by the leading term of the divisor.

The quotient starts with \(4 x^{2}\).

Final answer: \(4\).
blocks.hint: Divide the leading term of the dividend by the leading term of the divisor.

sections.title: How do I finish the quotient?
sections.label: Complete
sections.intro: Line up terms of the same degree. Keep a zero place for a missing term so terms remain aligned.

blocks.html: Continue until the leftover polynomial has smaller degree than the divisor.

blocks.prompt:
The polynomial \(P(x)=3 x^{3} - 12 x^{2} + 4 x - 12\) is divided by \(x - 4\).

Find the complete quotient.
blocks.solution:
Subtract the product of the divisor and the first quotient term. Repeat for the remaining leading terms.

The identity is \(P(x)=(x - 4)(3 x^{2} + 4)+4\).

Final answer: \(3 x^{2} + 4\).
blocks.hint: Subtract the product of the divisor and the first quotient term. Repeat for the remaining leading terms.

blocks.html: Subtract the whole product at every step.

blocks.prompt:
The polynomial \(P(x)=4 x^{3} - 15 x^{2} - 20\) is divided by \(x - 4\).

Find the complete quotient.
blocks.solution:
Subtract the product of the divisor and the first quotient term. Repeat for the remaining leading terms.

The identity is \(P(x)=(x - 4)(4 x^{2} + x + 4)-4\).

Final answer: \(4 x^{2} + x + 4\).
blocks.hint: Subtract the product of the divisor and the first quotient term. Repeat for the remaining leading terms.

sections.title: How can I check the division?
sections.label: Check
sections.intro: Multiply the divisor and quotient. Add the remainder to reconstruct the dividend.

blocks.html: \(P(x)=D(x)Q(x)+R\) when the divisor is linear.

blocks.prompt:
The polynomial \(P(x)=9 x^{3} - 18 x^{2} + 20 x - 26\) is divided by \(3 x - 5\).

State the remainder.
blocks.solution:
The remainder is the constant left when division can go no further.

The same result follows by evaluating \(P(\frac{5}{3})\) since the divisor is zero there.

Final answer: \(-1\).
blocks.hint: The remainder is the constant left when division can go no further.

blocks.html: A remainder can be a negative number.

blocks.prompt:
The polynomial \(P(x)=16 x^{3} - 20 x^{2} + 20 x - 25\) is divided by \(4 x - 5\).

State the remainder.
blocks.solution:
The remainder is the constant left when division can go no further.

The same result follows by evaluating \(P(\frac{5}{4})\) since the divisor is zero there.

Final answer: \(0\).
blocks.hint: The remainder is the constant left when division can go no further.

addmaths-0606-factors-polynomials-known-.description: Translate a known factor into a substitution equation, then factor further.

sections.title: Which input should I substitute?
sections.label: Use zero
sections.intro: Set the stated linear factor equal to zero to find the correct input.

blocks.html: \(x-a\) is a factor if and only if \(P(a)=0\).

blocks.prompt:
The polynomial \(P(x)=k x^{2} + 2 x^{3} + 4 x - 8\) has \(x + 2\) as a factor.

Find \(k\).
blocks.solution:
If a linear expression is a factor, the polynomial is zero at the root of that expression.

Use \(P(-2)=0\). This gives \(4 k - 32=0\).

Final answer: \(8\).
blocks.hint: If a linear expression is a factor, the polynomial is zero at the root of that expression.

blocks.html: Use the root of the factor, rather than the constant as it appears in the factor.

blocks.prompt:
The polynomial \(P(x)=k x^{2} + 3 x^{3} + 11 x - 12\) has \(x + 3\) as a factor.

Find \(k\).
blocks.solution:
If a linear expression is a factor, the polynomial is zero at the root of that expression.

Use \(P(-3)=0\). This gives \(9 k - 126=0\).

Final answer: \(14\).
blocks.hint: If a linear expression is a factor, the polynomial is zero at the root of that expression.

sections.title: How do I find the remaining factor?
sections.label: Extract
sections.intro: After identifying the parameter, divide by the known factor. Multiply back as a check.

blocks.html: A cubic divided by one of its linear factors has a quadratic quotient.

blocks.prompt:
The polynomial \(P(x)=k x + 2 x^{3} - 9 x^{2} + 30\) has \(x - 6\) as a factor.

After finding \(k\), determine the quotient of \(P(x)\) by \(x - 6\).
blocks.solution:
Divide the complete polynomial by the stated linear factor.

Multiplying \(x - 6\) by the quotient must reproduce the cubic exactly.

Final answer: \(2 x^{2} + 3 x - 5\).
blocks.hint: Divide the complete polynomial by the stated linear factor.

blocks.html: Use the completed coefficients before dividing.

blocks.prompt:
The polynomial \(P(x)=k x + 3 x^{3} + x^{2} + 5\) has \(x - 1\) as a factor.

After finding \(k\), determine the quotient of \(P(x)\) by \(x - 1\).
blocks.solution:
Divide the complete polynomial by the stated linear factor.

Multiplying \(x - 1\) by the quotient must reproduce the cubic exactly.

Final answer: \(3 x^{2} + 4 x - 5\).
blocks.hint: Divide the complete polynomial by the stated linear factor.

sections.title: Does a new divisor always leave zero?
sections.label: Cross check
sections.intro: Only factors have zero remainder. Substitute the root of the new divisor before deciding.

blocks.html: A non-zero remainder proves that the new divisor is not a factor.

blocks.prompt:
The polynomial \(P(x)=k x^{2} + 2 x^{3} - 14 x + 24\) has \(x - 4\) as a factor.

Find the remainder when the completed polynomial is divided by \(x + 3\).
blocks.solution:
Substitute the value which makes the new divisor zero.

Evaluate \(P(-3)\) using the coefficient already found.

Final answer: \(-42\).
blocks.hint: Substitute the value which makes the new divisor zero.

blocks.html: Do not reuse the zero from a different divisor.

blocks.prompt:

blocks.solution:

Final answer: \(-270\).
blocks.hint: Substitute the value which makes the new divisor zero.

addmaths-0606-factors-polynomials-cubic-.description: Divide out the known linear factor and solve the entire quadratic factor.

sections.title: How does one root help solve the cubic?
sections.label: Reduce
sections.intro: Use the root to write down the corresponding linear factor, then divide the cubic.

blocks.html: An exact factor divides out without a remainder.

blocks.prompt:
The cubic is \(P(x)=2 x^{3} - 14 x^{2} - 32 x + 224\). It has a root at \(-4\).

Find the quadratic quotient after dividing out the stated linear factor.
blocks.solution:
Divide the cubic by the linear expression associated with the known root.

Use divisor \(x + 4\) and verify the quotient by multiplication.

Final answer: \(2 x^{2} - 22 x + 56\).
blocks.hint: Divide the cubic by the linear expression associated with the known root.

blocks.html: A root and its corresponding factor use opposite signs in the linear expression.

blocks.prompt:
The cubic is \(P(x)=3 x^{3} - 21 x^{2} - 84 x + 480\). It has a root at \(-5\).

Find the quadratic quotient after dividing out the stated linear factor.
blocks.solution:
Divide the cubic by the linear expression associated with the known root.

Use divisor \(x + 5\) and verify the quotient by multiplication.

Final answer: \(3 x^{2} - 36 x + 96\).
blocks.hint: Divide the cubic by the linear expression associated with the known root.

sections.title: What if the quotient has a repeated root?
sections.label: Repeat
sections.intro: Solve the quadratic part and add the root from the linear factor. List distinct values once.

blocks.html: Multiplicity describes how often a factor occurs, rather than how many distinct values it produces.

blocks.prompt:
The cubic is \(P(x)=3 x^{3} - 21 x^{2} - 15 x + 225\). It has a root at \(-3\).

Solve \(P(x)=0\) over the reals. Give distinct roots exactly.
blocks.solution:
Use the known root and solve the remaining quadratic.

The quadratic factor is \(3 x^{2} - 30 x + 75\). A repeated root is listed once.

Final answer: \(\{-3, 5\}\).
blocks.hint: Use the known root and solve the remaining quadratic.

retry.feedback: Check both the known factor and all roots of the quadratic quotient.

blocks.html: Do not leave out the root that was supplied in the question.

blocks.prompt:
The cubic is \(P(x)=x^{3} - 6 x^{2} - 15 x + 100\). It has a root at \(-4\).

How does one root help solve the cubic?

An exact factor divides out without a remainder.

What if the quotient has a repeated root?

Multiplicity describes how often a factor occurs, rather than how many distinct values it produces.

How do I keep irrational roots exact?

Include both square-root signs if they give distinct real values.

addmaths-0606-factors-polynomials-remain.description: Use evaluated remainders and two independent equations to recover coefficients.

sections.title: Why does substitution give a remainder?
sections.label: Evaluate
sections.intro: At the root of the divisor its product with the quotient is zero. The remainder is the only term left.

blocks.html: The remainder for division by \(ax+b\) is \(P(-b/a)\).

blocks.prompt:
Let \(P(x)=k x + m + 2 x^{3} + 9 x^{2} - 60 x - 32\). The remainders on division by \(2 x + 16\) and \(3 x - 12\) are \(-11\) and \(13\) respectively.

Find \(k\).
blocks.solution:
Apply the remainder theorem to both divisors and subtract the two equations.

Use \(-8k+m=-11\) and \(4k+m=13\).

Final answer: \(2\).
blocks.hint: Apply the remainder theorem to both divisors and subtract the two equations.

blocks.html: The input is the zero of the divisor, even if its leading coefficient is not one.

blocks.prompt:
Let \(P(x)=k x + m + 3 x^{3} - 4 x^{2} - 28 x - 16\). The remainders on division by \(2 x + 4\) and \(3 x - 12\) are \(-1\) and \(17\) respectively.

Find \(k\).
blocks.solution:
Apply the remainder theorem to both divisors and subtract the two equations.

Use \(-2k+m=-1\) and \(4k+m=17\).

Final answer: \(3\).
blocks.hint: Apply the remainder theorem to both divisors and subtract the two equations.

sections.title: How can two remainders identify two constants?
sections.label: Eliminate
sections.intro: Write one equation for each substitution. Subtract the equations to eliminate a common term.

blocks.html: Different divisor roots provide independent information about the unknowns.

blocks.prompt:
Let \(P(x)=k x + m + 3 x^{3} - 75 x\). The remainders on division by \(x + 5\) and \(x - 5\) are \(-24\) and \(36\) respectively.

Find \(m\).
blocks.solution:
Substitute k into either of the remainder equations.

Use the equation at \(-5\) with \(k=6\).

Final answer: \(6\).
blocks.hint: Substitute k into either of the remainder equations.

blocks.html: Set the polynomial equal to the stated remainder, rather than to zero by default.

blocks.prompt:

blocks.solution:

Final answer: \(6\).
blocks.hint: Substitute k into either of the remainder equations.

sections.title: How do I predict another remainder?
sections.label: New divisor
sections.intro: Use the recovered coefficients in the original polynomial and substitute at the new divisor root.

blocks.html: The same theorem works for each new linear divisor.

blocks.prompt:
Let \(P(x)=k x + m + x^{3} - 5 x^{2} - 8 x + 12\). The remainders on division by \(2 x + 4\) and \(3 x - 18\) are \(-1\) and \(31\) respectively.

Find the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x + 3\).
blocks.solution:
Use the completed coefficients and evaluate the polynomial where the new divisor is zero.

Evaluate \(P(-3)\).

Final answer: \(-41\).
blocks.hint: Use the completed coefficients and evaluate the polynomial where the new divisor is zero.
